2027-06-16.title: The Apostles' Fast begins · Wednesday of the fourth week after Pentecost
readings: Servants of Christ and stewards of God's mysteries
Jesus gives authority to the Twelve; the names of the twelve apostles
2027-06-16.alt: Season of Pentecost, the week after the Fourth Sunday after Pentecost. Today the Apostles' Fast (Shleeha Nombu) begins; it is kept until the feast of Sts Peter and Paul on 29 June, when the fast ends.
2027-06-16.verse: Moreover, it is required of stewards that they be found trustworthy.
theo: Today the Apostles' Fast begins. On Sunday the priests reminded us of it, as the Panchangam asked them to do, and from today until the feast of Sts Peter and Paul the Church keeps it. Why fast now, only a few weeks after the joy of Pentecost? Jesus himself gave the answer when he was asked why his disciples did not fast: “The wedding guests cannot mourn as long as the bridegroom is with them, can they? The days will come when the bridegroom is taken away from them, and then they will fast.” The Bridegroom has ascended to the Father; the Spirit has come; and now the Church, like the apostles, sets out on the long road of mission. The Acts of the Apostles shows how the first Christians did it. At Antioch, “while they were worshiping the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, ‘Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them.’” Then, after more fasting and prayer, they laid hands on them and sent them off. The fast of the apostles is a fast for mission: we deny ourselves a little so that the Church may be sent, and so that we ourselves may go where the Spirit sends us. St Leo the Great, preaching in Rome on the fast that followed Pentecost, told his people that after the days of holy rejoicing the Church fasts so that the gifts of the Spirit may be guarded by self-discipline, and he called it a fast handed down from the apostles (Sermons on the Fast of Pentecost, in substance). Our Orthodox brothers and sisters of the Malankara tradition keep this fast too, and it is good to know that in these days many Christians of our land are praying and fasting together.

The Gospel gives the fast its faces. “Then Jesus summoned his twelve disciples and gave them authority over unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to cure every disease and every sickness.” Then Matthew does something he rarely does: he writes out a list of names. “First, Simon, also known as Peter, and his brother Andrew; James son of Zebedee, and his brother John; Philip and Bartholomew; Thomas and Matthew the tax collector; James son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus; Simon the Cananaean, and Judas Iscariot, the one who betrayed him.” These are not titles but persons: two pairs of brothers from the fishing boats of Galilee, a tax collector who had worked for the hated ruling power, and a Simon whose surname probably marked him as a man of zeal, two men who might once have quarrelled bitterly, now seated at one table. Our own Mar Thoma is there, the apostle whom our fathers' faith remembers as the one who brought the Gospel to India. Bartholomew, whom the Panchangam remembered last week, and Thaddaeus, whom it will remember on Saturday, are there too. And the list ends with a name that should make every disciple humble: Judas, chosen like the others, who betrayed. Jesus chose these twelve and gave them his own authority; through them the Church is apostolic. Our bishops are their successors, and our priests share their work. In this fast we pray for them by name.

St Paul tells the Corinthians how to think of the apostles and of all who serve the Church: “Think of us in this way, as servants of Christ and stewards of God's mysteries. Moreover, it is required of stewards that they be found trustworthy.” A steward manages what belongs to someone else. The mysteries of God, the word, the sacraments, the Holy Qurbono which our tradition loves to call the holy mysteries, do not belong to the priest; he holds them in trust. St John Chrysostom, preaching on this passage, says that a steward does not treat his master's goods as his own, but distributes them faithfully, and so must every servant of the Church (Homilies on 1 Corinthians 10, in substance). And in a smaller way every Christian is a steward: of time, of money, of the body, of the faith received in Baptism. That is what the fast trains us for. When we fast, pray more and give alms, we learn that our food, our hours and our money are not simply ours. Paul adds a warning for the fast: “Therefore do not pronounce judgment before the time, before the Lord comes, who will bring to light the things now hidden in darkness and will disclose the purposes of the heart.” A fast that makes us harsh judges of others, especially of our priests, is no fast at all. Let these days make us trustworthy stewards, slow to judge and quick to pray.
outline: Ask: what will I give up in these days of the Apostles' Fast, and for whom will I offer it?
The Bridegroom has gone up; the Church fasts and is sent, as at Antioch.
Persons, not titles; Mar Thoma among them; our bishops their successors.
The mysteries are held in trust; fasting teaches stewardship and forbids rash judgement.
“It is required of stewards that they be found trustworthy.”
live: Decide today, alone or as a family, on one concrete fast for these days, according to the guidance of our Church, and set aside what it saves for someone in need.
Pray for the apostles of today (Matthew 10:1–4)
Each day of the fast, pray one Our Father for the Pope, one for your bishop and one for your parish priest, by name.
2027-06-16.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you called the Twelve by name, gave them your authority and sent them to proclaim your kingdom. As we begin the Apostles' Fast, strengthen us by your Holy Spirit to deny ourselves for the sake of your Gospel. Make us trustworthy stewards of your mysteries and of all you have entrusted to us. Keep us from judging before the time, and fill your Church with apostles who will carry your word to every nation. Bless our Holy Father the Pope, our bishops and our priests, the successors and helpers of your apostles. You live and reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: The holy mysteries entrusted to the apostles are placed on our altar in every Holy Qurbono: the priest, a steward and not an owner, offers the one sacrifice of Christ, and a fasting people receives the Bread that strengthens it for mission.
conn: Matthew 9:15: Jesus foretells that his disciples will fast when the Bridegroom is taken from them; the Church's fasts after the Ascension answer that word.
Acts 13:2–3: the Church of Antioch worships and fasts, the Spirit sets apart Barnabas and Saul, and after fasting and prayer they are sent.
A night of prayer before the choice.
Luke 6:12–16: Jesus spends the night in prayer before he chooses the Twelve and names them apostles.
fathers: After the days of Pentecost rejoicing, the Church keeps a fast handed down from the apostles, so that the gifts received from the Holy Spirit may be guarded by self-discipline (Sermons on the Fast of Pentecost, in substance).

A steward does not treat the goods of his master as his own but distributes them faithfully; so must everyone who serves in the Church, for what he handles belongs to God (Homilies on 1 Corinthians 10, in substance).
magis: The interior penance of the Christian can be expressed in many ways; Scripture and the Fathers insist above all on three forms: fasting, prayer and almsgiving.

The seasons and days of penance in the course of the liturgical year are intense moments of the Church's penitential practice, suited to spiritual exercises, voluntary self-denial and fraternal sharing.
The bishops, by divine institution, have succeeded to the place of the apostles as shepherds of the Church; whoever hears them hears Christ.

quick: Today the Apostles' Fast (Shleeha Nombu) begins; it ends with the feast of Sts Peter and Paul on 29 June.
Jesus gives the Twelve authority over unclean spirits and every sickness; Matthew lists their names.
St Paul: we are servants of Christ and stewards of God's mysteries, and stewards must be found trustworthy.
2027-06-16.action: Choose one concrete fast for these days and one person to whom you will give what it saves.
2027-06-16.question: What has God entrusted to me, and am I a trustworthy steward of it?

family.explain: Today the Apostles' Fast begins. Jesus chose twelve friends, called them by name, and sent them to tell everyone about God's love. One of them, St Thomas, came to our own land. The apostles prayed and fasted before they went out to preach. In these days we also give up something small, pray a little more and share with the poor, so that the Good News can reach many people.
family.intention: We pray for the Pope, for our bishop and for our parish priest, who carry on the work of the apostles.
family.ask: Ask: “What small thing can our family give up during this fast, and whom shall we help with it?”

illus: A family in Mavelikara sat down together on the evening before the Apostles' Fast to decide how to keep it. The father suggested the usual abstinence from meat and fish. The teenage son, after some hesitation, offered to give up the online games that ate up his evenings. The youngest daughter said she would keep the coins from her snack money in a tin. Then the grandmother asked: and for whom are we fasting? They decided on two things: the money would go towards the operation of a neighbour's child, and every night they would pray for the parish priest, who had been ill. On the feast of Sts Peter and Paul they opened the tin and counted the coins together. The amount was not large, but the neighbour wept when it was given, and the priest, recovered, came to bless the house.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, at the start of the Apostles' Fast we gather in your name. Give us the spirit of your apostles: prayer, self-denial and zeal for your Gospel. Amen.
share: Then Jesus summoned his twelve disciples and gave them authority (Matthew 10:1). How do I see the apostolic Church in my bishop and my parish?
Think of us in this way, as servants of Christ and stewards of God's mysteries (1 Corinthians 4:1). What has God entrusted to my care?
Do not pronounce judgment before the time (1 Corinthians 4:5). Whom do I judge too quickly?
interc: For the Holy Father, Pope Leo, successor of St Peter, and for all the bishops, successors of the apostles.
For our major archbishop, our bishops and all our priests, that they may be found trustworthy stewards of God's mysteries.
For missionaries in distant places, that the Spirit who sent Barnabas and Saul may strengthen them.
For all the Christians of Kerala who keep the Apostles' Fast in these days, that our prayer and fasting may draw us closer to one another.
For the poor who will receive the alms of this fast, that they may know the love of God.
pm.close: Lord God, your apostles fasted and prayed and were sent out by your Spirit. As we begin this fast, purify our hearts, make us trustworthy stewards of your gifts, keep us from judging others, and send us out as witnesses of your Son. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

term: The Apostles' Fast. Shleeha is the Syriac word for apostle (one who is sent) and nombu is the Malayalam word for a fast. Kept by the Churches of the Syriac tradition after Pentecost, it ends with the feast of Sts Peter and Paul on 29 June. In 2027 the Panchangam marks its beginning on 16 June.

homily: Dear friends, today the Apostles' Fast begins, and it will end with the feast of Sts Peter and Paul. Jesus said that when the bridegroom is taken away, his friends will fast (Matthew 9:15). The Lord has gone up to the Father and the Spirit has come. Now, like the apostles, we fast and pray so that the Church may go out with the Good News.

In the Gospel Jesus calls the Twelve and gives them authority over unclean spirits and every sickness (Matthew 10:1). Then we hear their names: Peter and Andrew, James and John, Philip and Bartholomew, Thomas and Matthew, James and Thaddaeus, Simon, and Judas who betrayed him (Matthew 10:2–4). Our own Mar Thoma is among them. Jesus does not choose an idea; he chooses persons. Our bishops are their successors today, and in this fast we pray for them.

St Paul says: think of us in this way, as servants of Christ and stewards of God's mysteries (1 Corinthians 4:1). A steward takes care of what belongs to his master. The holy mysteries do not belong to the priest; he holds them in trust. And we too are stewards of our time, our money and our faith. Fasting teaches us this. It is required of stewards that they be found trustworthy (1 Corinthians 4:2).

Paul also warns: do not pronounce judgment before the time (1 Corinthians 4:5). A fast that makes us harsh with others is not the fast of the apostles. So let us fast humbly, pray for our shepherds, give what we save to the poor, and leave judgment to the Lord. Amen.
kids: Children, today a special time of prayer begins: the Apostles' Fast. The apostles were Jesus' twelve special friends. He called each one by his name, Peter, John, Thomas and the others, and sent them to tell the whole world about God. Before they went, they prayed and fasted. During these days you can give up one sweet or one cartoon, and pray for our bishop and our priest. And the money you save for a chocolate can go to a child who needs it. That is how we help the apostles' work today.

intro: Theme: “It is required of stewards that they be found trustworthy.”
At the beginning of the Apostles' Fast: a fast for mission, the Twelve called by name, and the trustworthy stewards of God's mysteries.

sub: The priest at the altar, the parent at home.
q: Not so with my servant Moses; he is entrusted with all my house.
Like good stewards of the manifold grace of God, serve one another with whatever gift each of you has received.
points.apply: Make an honest list of what God has entrusted to you and choose one thing to use more faithfully during the fast.

sub: Fishermen, a tax collector, a zealot.
q: Do not fear, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by name, you are mine.
And when day came, he called his disciples and chose twelve of them, whom he also named apostles
points.apply: Pray each day of the fast for the Pope, your bishop and your parish priest by name.

sub: When the Bridegroom is taken away.
q: Yet even now, says the Lord, return to me with all your heart, with fasting, with weeping, and with mourning
While they were worshiping the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, “Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them.”
points.apply: Decide today on one fast, one daily prayer and one act of almsgiving for the whole Apostles' Fast.

concl: The Apostles' Fast is the Church's fast for mission: we deny ourselves so that the Gospel may go out.
The Twelve were stewards of the mysteries; in our measure, so are we.
2027-06-16.resolve: Keep the Apostles' Fast humbly and faithfully, praying for the successors of the apostles and judging no one before the time.
